minutes.headline: Select Board heard the 30 School Street park plan and FY23 preliminary budget, and put off a decision on tax-lien parcels.
minutes.summary: The board heard the landscape architect's final master plan and phasing costs for the 30 School Street park and agreed to put at least two warrant articles on the town meeting warrant. The town manager presented the FY23 preliminary budget, and the board discussed whether four parcels should be pulled from the March tax lien sale at the open space committee's request, deferring any decision. The only vote was adjournment.

public_comment.topic: A resident and parks commission member praised the 30 School Street design, urged doing the project all at once, not cheapening it, and suggested solar panels on the pavilion roof.
A resident and finance committee member backed delaying the tax lien decision, favored open space, raised the service costs of development, and asked for a clear analysis of foreclosure versus sale.

what_happened.line: The Select Board made no decision on four tax-lien parcels the open space committee asked to pull; advertising of the March sale proceeds and the talks continue.
The board agreed to prepare at least two warrant articles for the 30 School Street park, covering demolition/abatement and remaining design costs.
The landscape architect presented the final master plan and four-phase cost estimate, and the chair said phase one abatement and demolition will be done regardless of the park.
The town manager presented the FY23 preliminary budget, which fully funds the school superintendent's budget and the Monty Tech minimum assessment increase.
The town manager announced the DPW director's resignation, effective March 11, and said the position will be advertised.

why_it_matters: The 30 School Street warrant articles and the school and Monty Tech funding in the FY23 budget are the items voters will be asked to approve at town meeting.
Whether the four parcels are sold or pulled decides if the town collects back taxes, fees and interest or gives up that money and keeps land that may later face foreclosure costs.
watch_next: Warrant article wording for 30 School Street, to be discussed at the next meetings before the warrant closes.
The final decision on pulling the four parcels from the March tax lien sale, with written reasoning requested from the open space committee.

The main differences are how the 30 School Street warrant articles are described, how the tax lien outcome is described, the school budget figure (673,617 in ours, 541K in the official), and a set of attendees our minutes missed.
